title: All-Inclusive Holidays in Dubrovnik 2027: Prices & Hotels
metaDescription: Does Dubrovnik have all-inclusive hotels? Yes, a few. See what is included, per-person prices vs half-board and apartments, and who should skip it.
content:
## Does Dubrovnik Have All-Inclusive Hotels?

Yes, but only a handful. Dubrovnik is a city-break destination, so most hotels sell bed and breakfast or half-board. All-inclusive is concentrated in the resort-style hotels on the Babin Kuk peninsula, about 5 km northwest of the Old Town, and on one island resort a short ferry ride away.

Hotels that currently sell all-inclusive packages:

- **Sunny Dubrovnik by Valamar** (Iva Dulčića, Babin Kuk): 3-star, family-focused, with an outdoor pool and a children's pool. This is the budget entry point.
- **Valamar Lacroma Dubrovnik** (Babin Kuk): 4-star, large buffet-style resort.
- **President Hotel, Valamar Collection** (Babin Kuk): 4-star, sea-front, the highest-rated all-inclusive option in the city.
- **TUI BLUE Kalamota Island Resort** (Koločep island): beachfront, reached by a ferry of roughly 30 minutes from Dubrovnik.

All-inclusive is often a seasonal rate plan rather than a fixed offer. Some of these hotels sell it only on selected dates or as a board upgrade, so check the board type on the booking page before paying.

The five-star hotels in the Old Town and on the Lapad and Ploče coast, such as Hilton Imperial, Excelsior and the Royal Hotels, sell room-and-breakfast or half-board. They do not sell all-inclusive.

## What Is Included in All-Inclusive in Dubrovnik?

Typical inclusions:

- Breakfast, lunch and dinner, usually as buffets, with themed evenings.
- Snacks and ice cream in the afternoon.
- House drinks with meals: local wine, beer, soft drinks, water, coffee.
- House drinks at the pool or lobby bar during set hours, usually about 10:00 to 23:00.
- Kids' club, animation programme and use of pools.

Not normally included:

- Premium spirits, imported brands and cocktails from the à la carte menu.
- Restaurant meals outside the hotel.
- Sunbeds on public beaches, spa treatments and excursions.
- Tourist tax (roughly €1–2 per person per night, children discounted) and parking.

The lower-end all-inclusive plans are better described as full-board plus drinks. Read the board description for the exact hours and drinks list.

## All-Inclusive Prices per Person per Night (2027 Estimate)

These are approximate ranges for two adults sharing a double room. Rates move strongly with dates, so treat them as a planning guide, not a quote.

| Option | Peak (July–August) | Shoulder (May–June, Sept–Oct) |
|---|---|---|
| All-inclusive, 3–4★ Babin Kuk | €90–170 | €55–95 |
| Half-board, same hotels | €75–140 | €45–80 |
| Half-board, Old Town 4–5★ | €120–250 | €70–140 |
| Private apartment, room only | €45–75 | €30–50 |
| Apartment plus food (self-catered and eating out) | €70–115 | €55–85 |

The gap between half-board and all-inclusive is usually only €10–30 per person per night. That small premium is what makes all-inclusive worth considering for families, since drinks and lunches add up quickly. Dubrovnik restaurant prices are among the highest in Croatia. A pizza or pasta lunch costs about €12–18, and a main course in the Old Town often runs €20–35.

Children under 6–7 usually stay free or at a heavy discount when sharing with two adults. Children aged 7–12 are often discounted by roughly 50%. This is where all-inclusive pays off most.

## Who Should Book All-Inclusive in Dubrovnik

**Families with small children.** Fixed meal times, a kids' club, a children's pool and no restaurant bills make logistics easy. Babin Kuk also has flat promenades suited to strollers, and the Lapad beaches are nearby.

**Short stays of 3–5 nights.** A package deal for a few nights (a three-night stay was available for about €450 in the shoulder season) is cheaper than eating out daily. It also removes the need to plan.

**Travellers who mainly want a pool and a beach.** Public beaches such as Banje charge roughly €60 for two sunbeds and a parasol in autumn, while hotel sunbeds are free for guests.

## Who Is Better Off Self-Catering

**Sightseers.** All-inclusive hotels at Babin Kuk are about 5 km from the Old Town. A bus ride takes 15–25 minutes, and taxis cost roughly €12–20 each way. If you plan to walk the walls, take the Elaphiti cruise and eat in town, you pay for meals you will skip.

**Stays of a week or more.** Buffet menus repeat. Guest feedback on the larger resorts commonly calls the food repetitive and lukewarm, and that wears thin after day four.

**Groups of friends and larger families.** A two-bedroom apartment with a kitchen, with groceries from Konzum or Tommy supermarkets, works out noticeably cheaper per head.

The all-inclusive wristband looks like the cheap option in July, but for anyone who wants to see the Old Town it usually turns into a bill for meals not eaten and taxis taken.

## Insider Tips

- Book shoulder season (late May, June, September) when all-inclusive prices can drop by 40–50% compared with peak weeks.
- Choose half-board plus a hotel with a nearby supermarket if you want flexibility at lunch. Lunch is the meal most people skip.
- On Koločep, the hotel is effectively the only large dining option. Last ferries limit evening trips to town, so confirm the timetable before booking.
- Ask whether all-inclusive drinks cover the beach bar and pool bar, or only the main restaurant.
- Apartments in Lapad and Babin Kuk cost less than in the Old Town and sit near the same beaches.

## Nearby Alternatives

TUI BLUE Kalamota Island Resort on Koločep is the closest all-inclusive outside the Babin Kuk cluster. Beyond the city, all-inclusive hotels are more common further along the Adriatic coast, but the Dubrovnik area has the options above.

faq.question: Are there all-inclusive resorts in Dubrovnik?
faq.answer: Yes, a few. Sunny Dubrovnik by Valamar, Valamar Lacroma Dubrovnik and President Hotel, Valamar Collection sell all-inclusive plans on Babin Kuk, and TUI BLUE Kalamota Island Resort sells them on Koločep. Always check the board type for your dates.

faq.question: How much does all-inclusive cost in Dubrovnik per person?
faq.answer: Roughly €90–170 per person per night in July and August and €55–95 in May, June, September and October, based on two adults sharing. Children's discounts are significant.

faq.question: Is all-inclusive cheaper than half-board in Dubrovnik?
faq.answer: No, it costs about €10–30 more per person per night. It only works out cheaper overall if you eat lunch at the hotel and drink several times a day, which is typical for families with small children.

faq.question: Is all-inclusive worth it in Dubrovnik?
faq.answer: It is worth it for families and short beach-focused stays. It is poor value if you spend your days in the Old Town and eat out.

faq.question: Is an apartment cheaper than all-inclusive in Dubrovnik?
faq.answer: Usually yes, especially for stays of a week or more or for groups. A room-only apartment can cost about €45–75 per person in peak season, but eating out raises the total to roughly €70–115.

faq.question: Where is the nearest all-inclusive to the Old Town?
faq.answer: The Babin Kuk hotels, about 5 km from the Old Town, are the closest. TUI BLUE Kalamota on Koločep is about 30 minutes away by ferry.

quickAnswer: Dubrovnik has a small number of real all-inclusive hotels, mainly Valamar properties on the Babin Kuk peninsula, plus TUI BLUE Kalamota Island Resort on Koločep. Expect roughly €90–170 per person per night in peak season and €55–95 in shoulder season. It suits families with small children on short stays; self-catering suits longer, flexible trips.
